idea.title: Don't seal a teammate into a pocket: a move that takes the last way out of a closed pocket from a visible teammate inside it costs P.friendExitPenalty when another move keeps it, judged by the teammate's timed fill, not only its next step
idea.hypothesis: watch.py doom (orch/death-mechanism, MISSES 64) on result-blind Queen Of Spades games of 8636 and 8473, per game ours against theirs: against dev teams pocket deaths doomed by a teammate's body are 16.3 v 4.3 (16 games, sign p 0.002); against ladder teams 11.3 v 10.6 (37 games, even). In game 403920 dragon 57 was doomed at r135 when teammate 51's split child was born on the pocket's only way out, and 8 of our 35 deaths were teammate dooms in the pocket. Safety::blocksTeammateExit (P.guardTeammateExit) only checks whether our move takes a teammate head's one remaining neighbour this turn, so a move (or split) that leaves the teammate a neighbour but no way out of the pocket passes. General quantity: our deaths whose doom trigger is a teammate's body, per game, by place (pocket or open) and map. Measure first on those doom rows (watch.py doom --json): for each, which teammate move closed the way out (entering, eating, turning deeper, splitting) and whether that teammate had a legal move that kept the doomed dragon's timed fill reaching the exit. Stop only if fewer than a quarter of the teammate dooms had such an alternative at chance.rates_p <= 0.1; otherwise build: with a visible teammate head inside a closed pocket (farmEntryOk's closed region or a portal's landing region), a move or split after which that teammate's timed fill (all bodies timed, as I537's gate) reaches no exit costs P.friendExitPenalty when another move keeps one, behind its own switch (P.guardTeammatePocket). Choices: every closed pocket on every map; splits count as moves (the child's body is the closer); state the share of teammate dooms in the open it leaves out. Prerequisite: I537 (E0208) builds the timed fill with all bodies timed; reuse it.

session.summary:
I committed the change as `0bd1a11`. The pocket deaths it targets fell in my own games, but not by enough to be sure it will pass the referee's target test (it needs p ≤ 0.01; mine read p 0.11).

**What changed** (`bot/seal.hpp`, wired into `evaluateMoves` in `bot/scoring.hpp`, behind the new switch `P.guardTeammatePocket`):
- For each teammate in view, the bot now floods the space that teammate can still reach after each of our four possible steps, timing every body by when its tail frees the tile.
- A step after which the teammate has no way out costs `P.friendExitPenalty`, but only when another step of ours that is safe for us keeps its way out. So our only safe step is never refused.
- The older guard (`Safety::blocksTeammateExit`) only checked the teammate's very next step. A step that pays that guard's penalty isn't charged again.

**Measured before building:**
- Champion games on 41 generated and 28 renamed off-generator maps with portal rooms (69 self-play, 138 against swarm): 849 deaths where a teammate's body shut one of ours into a pocket.
- In 247 of them (29%), the teammate that closed the way out was within view, didn't cross a portal, and had a legal step that kept both dragons free. That is above the idea's one-quarter stop line, so I built it.

**Results.** Candidate vs champion, each against swarm on the same 138 map-and-seat pairs:

| Build | Pocket teammate  [...] ment:**
- The target test may fall short: p 0.11 over 138 seats against one opponent is well off 0.01. Most remaining counted deaths are sealed by a teammate on the far side of a portal, which vision can't reach.
- A follow-up would share over sonar the portal landings that teammates inside a room depend on.
- Split children closing a way out are the other left-out case (4%).
- Measurement scripts and replays are in `data/` (gitignored).

Blocked by: vision stops at portals, so a dragon standing on a room's landing tile can't see the teammate it is sealing in (30% of counted deaths).

idea.title: Quick fix of E0239: Stand beside an equal enemy head only where we would ram it ourselves: the priced ram guard marks a drop-race tie risky (quick fix on E0239)
idea.hypothesis: E0239's coder built this fix in its follow-on turn (E0239: kept, SPRT accepted, est +10.8). Defect: Safety::badRammer's equal-head test called a drop-race tie safe; in 240 logging games v swarm, rammer and the old champion, standing there was rammed and lost 189 v 66 rams (n = 255, p = 3.2e-15). Fetch it and cherry-pick only its commits: `git fetch -q --no-tags /Users/me/Dev/unsw-battlecode-2026 fix/E0239 && git cherry-pick fadc209ba725a37685d7c78e408c9c508d566fd3..FETCH_HEAD`; resolve any conflict keeping both the fix and the champion's change, rerun the bot tests and the quick check, and change nothing else. Its coder's reasoning: General quantity: the swing of enemy-started head-ons on our dragons that stood beside an equal enemy head, by our drop-race edge there (dropHarvestEdge: drop tiles our other heads reach first less theirs). E0239 mirrored our even-ram gate symmetrically, so an equal head counted as a bad rammer only at a drop-race edge of -P.evenTradeMinHarvest or worse. In a logging copy of E0239's candidate (240 games: 40 fresh eval maps, both sides, against swarm, rammer and the old champion), standing beside an equal head at a tie (edge 0) was rammed within a round and lost against all three opponents: per row stood -0.32 (edge >= 0) and -1.03 (edge < 0) against the old champion, -0.71/-1.62 against rammer and -0.39/-1.50 against swarm. That is 189 losing rams against 66 winning (sign p 3e-15), and at edge < 0 alone 53 v 9 (p 5e-9). At +1 it was about even (-0.10, +0.33, -0.47 a row); at -1 or worse it was already risky. The head that starts a head-on wins a tie, matching the ram model's positive bias (P.ramWBias). The fix: an equal head's reach is risky unless dropHarvestEdge >= P.evenTradeMinHarvest, the same bar our own ram needs. It reuses that param and adds no cutoff. It fires on 1.5-3.1 stood tie rows a game in those games. E0239's SPRT also read swarm 0.494 against 0.514-0.527 for the other four opponents (paired z -2.88 over trials); the tie rows lose against every opponent, so this is not opponent-specific. Scenarios: one against one, nobody near the drop: the tile beside the equal head is avoided; our teammate reaches more of the drop first: it is taken; their other head reaches the drop first: avoided.

Marked next.

- **Stale comments:** fixed the ones that still described the old mirror-image rule, in `bot/params.hpp`, `test_safety.cpp` and `test_decisions.cpp`.

Choices: same scope as E0239 (enemy heads one step from the tile, p [...] ep escape check in `escape.hpp`); the threshold reuses `P.evenTradeMinHarvest`, so no new cutoffs (`cutoffs.py`: 0 added); the tie cases occur 1.5-3.1 times a game in E0239's logging games. I ran no new shadow count, since this is a quick fix of a defect already measured.
